interpretation_notes: What passed: the campaign itself. C2 (job 768) counted under section 6.1, with COMPLETED 0:0 confirmed by both records, gates passed, qcow2 unchanged and nothing leaked or unreadable. It ran exactly the registered realized order (seed 42, 100 entries x 5, screenshot, N = 1, attempt 1) from a content-verified export of a9948ee, after all three ledger rows. All 8 predicted failures failed 5 of 5 by the mechanisms the prediction file names. 91 of the 92 predicted passes passed 5 of 5 under C2's rule, including every click, drag and hold on buttons 1-3, type_shell_hostile, type_symbols_shifted, key_menu, key_kp_add and caps_lock_roundtrip.

What failed and why: C2 failed, and I reproduced the verdict byte for byte. chord_super_d, listed in the prediction as a notable pass, failed 5 of 5. pyautogui.hotkey('winleft','d') produced the right four key events on the right keycodes, so the prediction's stated reason ('winleft' maps to Super_L, keycode 133) held. But the d press reached X with modifier state 0 within 1 ms of the Super_L press, losing Mod4 and also Mod2/NumLock. C2's registered rule (design decision 34) leaves out the modifier state of key releases only, so a press-state loss counts. Section 8 makes any deviation in either direction invalidate the suite for v1.

What this licenses: q2-action-path-v1 is invalid as a suite. No acceptance (A1-A7, the ladder) may be claimed under v1. Stage-1 GPU episodes stay blocked under this suite. The counted campaign may not be rerun (section 6.1), and a failed validity control is not repaired within v1 (section 11). A corrected prediction or C2 rule can enter only a new preregistration (section 8). Not submitting C1 and C3 after C2 failed is consistent with this. Because they were never run, v1 provides no C1 or C3 evidence, and a v2 must score them afresh.

What this does not license: it says nothing that L0-fixed or the Stage-1 harnesses (H-OSW-fixed, H-GA) are defective. C2 tests whether the suite's authors could predict the raw PyAutoGUI transport (L0-raw), not the project's executor, which holds keys 0.1 s and settles after each action. It also does not show any key-name or button-name claim in the prediction to be wrong. Every named mapping held, and the miss is in modifier timing on a desktop-shortcut chord. The investigation may be reported but cannot rescue v1. A v2 rule written after seeing this run (for example, excusing press states on shell-grabbed chords) is informed by this data and must say so.

Surprising: the symptom is identical to the one design decision 31 attributed to the master-keyboard switch on a session's first key (d press with state 0, runs 549 and 574). Here it appears in every repetition, even though every session ran the keyboard warm-up and chord_super_d was never the first trial. So decision 31's mechanism is at least incomplete under PyAutoGUI's transport. It is the same family as the release-state loss that decision 34 excused (chord_alt_f4: F4 release state 0 while the later Alt_L release has state 24 again), which suggests a shell keybinding grab during a fast chord. Decision 34's rationale ('the shell may be grabbing the keyboard for a side effect') covers this case, but its rule excused releases only, so the carve-out was narrower than its own reasoning. Whether L0-fixed is exposed is a Stage-1 risk question for v2: L0-fixed passed chord_super_d after the warm-up in development, but that is seed-42 development evidence, not acceptance.

Deviations, all disclosed and none affecting the verdict: (1) manifest host paths moved after rendering, which I reproduced exactly; (2) the C2 manifest also pins the executor addendum; (3) the operator scripts were reformatted after the run, with formatting-only diffs and outputs I reproduced byte for byte. VM time was 0.17 VM-hours CPU-only against the 0.25 sized, and no GPU was used.
